A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have characterized the set of all performance vectors that can be achieved by any priority discipline, and we have characterized the performance vector that can be achieved under the nonpreemptive last come first served (LCFS) priority discipline.

, for a wide class of priority disciplines, the performance vector can be controlled to achieve any desired vector in a specified convex set, and that the set is a convex polytope with a finite number of extreme points.

The main takeaway from our work is that
for the M/G/c queue system with J distinct customer classes, the achievable performance vector under nonpreempt priority rules is a convex set in J-dimensional Euclidean space.

the performance vector of the M/G/c queue with multiple customer classes is a convex function of the vector of priorities of the customer classes, and that the set of achievable performance vectors under any nonpreemptive scheduling discipline is a polytope.
the achievable performance vector is characterized by a set of linear equations, which can be solved numerically for the optimal performance vector and the corresponding optimal priority rule.
